title: Six-hour clock offsets kept four joint-exposure contrasts positive in North Wales domes in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested whether an assumed clock offset between ozone and weather records can remove joint-exposure contrasts. We used complete August and September 2021 hourly grids from a North Wales wildflower experiment. Fixed weather support and a common integer ozone offset from -6 to +6 hours kept four high-target heated-minus-ambient contrasts positive at cutoffs of 2 kPa vapor pressure deficit and 60 ppb ozone. Recorded-alignment contrasts were 43 to 92 hours. Their minimum values within six hours were 7 to 37 hours. Offsets of 9 to 11 hours first reduced them to zero. All 1,350 aggregate rows passed an independent scalar check. These are deterministic sensitivity ranges, not confidence intervals or measured clock errors. The records overlap prior campaign studies; the clock-offset test is new. One site-year, one dome per treatment, shared ambient weather, unknown gap filling and the assumed common offset limit inference. No plant injury or biodiversity effect was tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Joint-exposure contrasts over integer ozone offsets on fixed weather support. Ranges describe assumed offsets, not sampling uncertainty.
